Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 50968 of 2023
Applicant :- Babalu @ Arjun
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Badan Maurya
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA-I, for the State, apprised the Court that notice has been served to the informant of the case on 28.11.2023.
2. Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Ram Badan Maurya, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA-I, for the State.
4.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in S.T.No. 666 of 2023 arising out of Case Crime No.131 of 2023, under Sections 363,
366 and 376 IPC and Section 6 POCSO Act, Police Station Ganjdundwara, District Kasganj during pendency of the trial.

sentences.text:
FIR of the present case was lodged against six persons (non applicant) and from the perusal of the FIR it appears that it was lodged against the husband of the victim and his family members with regard to torture and demand of dowry and according to the FIR, victim, daughter of the informant,
had missed from her matrimonial home.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that initially FIR of the present case was lodged under Sections 498A and 364 IPC against the husband of the victim and her in-laws and admittedly victim is a married girl but during investigation applicant has been made accused in the present matter on the basis of call details of the victim.

7. He further submits that victim, i.e., daughter of the informant did not even disclose the name of the applicant either in her statements recorded under Sections 161 or 164 Cr.P.C. but it appears that as she was pregnant, therefore, when on the basis of her call details it reflects that she used to talk with the applicant then applicant was arrested and as per allegation he confessed his guilt.
8. He further submits that on the basis of false allegation applicant has been made accused in the present matter and there is no cogent evidence against him on record.
9. He further submits that even as per school record, victim was about 17-1/2 years old and according to CMO concerned, she was about 19 years old.

10. He further submits that victim is married lady aged about more than 18 years old and, therefore,
possibility cannot be ruled out that she would have conceived with her husband.
11. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 26.6.2023.
12. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant.
13. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

14. It is a peculiar case in which FIR was lodged against the husband of the victim and his family members under Sections 498-A and 364 IPC and victim, i.e., daughter of the informant when recovered then she did not make any allegation against the applicant in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. but from the record it reflects that as she was pregnant and she in her statement recorded during investigation stated that she did not like her husband and she never developed any physical relationship with him and, therefore, her call details were obtained and from her mobile it revealed that she used to talk with the applicant and thereafter name of applicant was surfaced in the present matter.
15. As victim did not make any allegation against the applicant either for making physical relationship or committing rape, therefore, no presumption, merely on the basis of call details of the victim, can be drawn at this stage that she became pregnant with the applicant.

sentences.text: Further, even as per school record victim appears to be aged about 17-1/2 years and as per CMO concerned her radiological age was around 19 years, therefore, possibility also cannot be ruled out that she was major.

17. Even considering the fact that her parents solemnized her marriage with some other person, and she was having affair with the applicant and due to societal fear or stigma she did not disclose his name in her statements recorded under Sections 161and 164 Cr.P.C., then also at this stage it cannot be said that against her wishes applicant either committed rape upon her or made physical relationship with her.
18. Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 26.6.2023.

19. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
20. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant-Babalu @Arjun be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
22.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

23. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 15.12.2023 SKM  Babalu @ Arjun vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44302066/
